## Connection Between EM and SmoothEM

Like the classical EM algorithm, the SmoothEM algorithm monotonically increases a posterior objective and hence converges to a local optimum.

### Theorem (Monotonicity of SmoothEM)

Let $\hat{\mathbf{U}}^{(i)}$ denote the estimate of the mean vectors at the $i$th iteration. Then
\[
P\!\big(\hat{\mathbf{U}}^{(i)} \mid \mathbf{X}\big) \;\ge\; 
P\!\big(\hat{\mathbf{U}}^{(i-1)} \mid \mathbf{X}\big).
\]


### Proof

Define the (unnormalized) log-posterior of $\mathbf{U}$ given $\mathbf{X}$ as
\[
I(\mathbf{U}) \;=\; \log P(\mathbf{X}\mid \mathbf{U}) \;+\; \log P(\mathbf{U}).
\]

At iteration $i$, define the evidence lower bound (ELBO) as
\[
\mathrm{ELBO}^{(i-1)}(\mathbf{U})
\;=\;
\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Z}\mid \mathbf{X},\,\hat{\mathbf{U}}^{(i-1)}}
\!\left[ \log P(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Z}\mid \mathbf{U}) \right] -
\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Z}\mid \mathbf{X},\,\hat{\mathbf{U}}^{(i-1)}}
\!\left[ \log P(\mathbf{Z}\mid \mathbf{X},\hat{\mathbf{U}}^{(i-1)}) \right].
\]

**Step 1. Variational lower bound.**  
For any distribution $q(\mathbf{z})$ and parameter $\mathbf{U}$, we have
\[
\log P(\mathbf{X}\mid \mathbf{U})
=
\mathbb{E}_{q(\mathbf{z})}\!\left[\log P(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{z}\mid \mathbf{U})\right]
-
\mathbb{E}_{q(\mathbf{z})}\!\left[\log q(\mathbf{z})\right]
+
\KL\!\left(q(\mathbf{z})\,\big\|\,P(\mathbf{z}\mid \mathbf{X},\mathbf{U})\right).
\]
Define the surrogate objective at iteration $i$:
\[
\tilde{I}^{(i)}(\mathbf{U})
\;=\;
\mathrm{ELBO}^{(i)}(\mathbf{U}) + \log P(\mathbf{U}),
\]
which satisfies $\tilde{I}(\mathbf{U}) \le I(\mathbf{U})$ for all $\mathbf{U}$, since \(\KL(\cdot)\ge 0\).

**Step 2. E-step.**  
Set
\[
q^{(i-1)}(\mathbf{z})
=
P(\mathbf{z}\mid \mathbf{X},\hat{\mathbf{U}}^{(i-1)}).
\]
Then by the lemma below,
\[
\KL\!\left(q^{(i-1)}(\mathbf{z})\,\big\|\,P(\mathbf{z}\mid \mathbf{X},\hat{\mathbf{U}}^{(i-1)})\right)=0,
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
\tilde{I}^{(i-1)}(\hat{\mathbf{U}}^{(i-1)}) = I(\hat{\mathbf{U}}^{(i-1)}).
\]

**Step 3. M-step.**  
Update
\[
\hat{\mathbf{U}}^{(i)} = \arg\max_{\mathbf{U}} \tilde{I}^{(i-1)}(\mathbf{U}),
\]
so that
\[
\tilde{I}^{(i-1)}(\hat{\mathbf{U}}^{(i)}) \;\ge\; \tilde{I}(\hat{\mathbf{U}}^{(i-1)}).
\]

**Step 4. Combine.**  
By construction,
\[
I(\hat{\mathbf{U}}^{(i)})
\;\ge\;
\tilde{I}^{(i-1)}(\hat{\mathbf{U}}^{(i)})
\;\ge\;
\tilde{I}^{(i-1)}(\hat{\mathbf{U}}^{(i-1)})
=
I(\hat{\mathbf{U}}^{(i-1)}).
\]
Thus, SmoothEM monotonically increases the posterior objective. $\blacksquare$

### Remark

The argument mirrors standard EM. SmoothEM simply adds a **smoothness prior** via $\log P(\mathbf{U})$, so the target changes from the log-likelihood $\log P(\mathbf{X}\mid \mathbf{U})$ to the log-posterior $I(\mathbf{U})$. The monotonicity proof is unchanged.



-------


### Lemma (Variational Lower Bound Decomposition)

For any distribution $q(\mathbf{z})$, the marginal likelihood can be decomposed as
\[
\log P(\mathbf{X}\mid \mathbf{U})
= \mathrm{ELBO}(q,\mathbf{U})
+ \mathrm{KL}\!\big(q(\mathbf{z}) \,\|\, P(\mathbf{z}\mid \mathbf{X},\mathbf{U})\big),
\]
where
\[
\mathrm{ELBO}(q,\mathbf{U})
= \mathbb{E}_{q(\mathbf{z})}\!\big[\log P(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{z}\mid \mathbf{U}) - \log q(\mathbf{z})\big].
\]

---

**Proof.**

Start from the marginal likelihood:
\[
\log P(\mathbf{X}\mid \mathbf{U})
= \log \frac{P(\mathbf{X}, \mathbf{z} \mid \mathbf{U})}{P(\mathbf{z}\mid \mathbf{X}, \mathbf{U})} = \log \frac{P(\mathbf{X}, \mathbf{z} \mid \mathbf{U})}{q(\mathbf{z})} \frac{q(\mathbf{z})}{P(\mathbf{z}\mid \mathbf{X}, \mathbf{U})}.
\]


Therefore with expectation over any distribution $q(\mathbf{z})$:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\log P(\mathbf{X}\mid \mathbf{U})
&= \mathbb{E}_{q(\mathbf{z})}\!\left[\log P(\mathbf{X}\mid \mathbf{U})\right] \\
&= \mathbb{E}_{q(\mathbf{z})}\!\left[\log \frac{P(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{z}\mid \mathbf{U})}{P(\mathbf{z}\mid \mathbf{X},\mathbf{U})}\right] \\
&= \mathbb{E}_{q(\mathbf{z})}\!\left[\log \frac{P(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{z}\mid \mathbf{U})}{q(\mathbf{z})} \cdot \frac{q(\mathbf{z})}{P(\mathbf{z}\mid \mathbf{X},\mathbf{U})}\right] \\
&= \mathbb{E}_{q(\mathbf{z})}\!\left[\log \frac{P(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{z}\mid \mathbf{U})}{q(\mathbf{z})}\right]
+ \mathbb{E}_{q(\mathbf{z})}\!\left[\log \frac{q(\mathbf{z})}{P(\mathbf{z}\mid \mathbf{X},\mathbf{U})}\right] \\
&= \mathrm{ELBO}(q,\mathbf{U})
+ \mathrm{KL}\!\big(q(\mathbf{z}) \,\|\, P(\mathbf{z}\mid \mathbf{X},\mathbf{U})\big).
\end{aligned}
\]

This establishes the decomposition. $\blacksquare$
